categories.main_business_segments: United Super Markets Holdings Inc. (USMH) operates primarily in the supermarket business, focusing on food retail through its group companies such as Maruetsu, Kasumi, Maxvalu Kanto, and Inageya. The group also engages in supporting businesses including food processing, logistics, real estate, product development, quality control, staffing, and facility management. The supermarket segment accounts for the overwhelming majority of revenue, with other businesses considered immaterial in scale.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The group leverages centralized procurement, logistics, and IT systems to optimize store operations and supply chain efficiency. It operates food processing centers (e.g., Maruetsu Soka Delica Center) for in-house production of prepared foods and original brands. Automation technologies such as electronic shelf labels and self-checkout systems are being introduced to improve productivity and customer experience.
categories.primary_customers_markets: USMH primarily serves general consumers in the Tokyo metropolitan area and surrounding regions, targeting households seeking daily groceries, fresh foods, and daily necessities. Its supermarkets cater to a wide demographic, including families, seniors, and working individuals, with a focus on convenience, quality, and value.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are concentrated in the Tokyo metropolitan area and adjacent prefectures, making it the largest supermarket group in the region. All stores and facilities are located in Japan, with no significant overseas operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: USMH operates at the downstream end of the supply chain as a retailer, directly serving end consumers. Through its subsidiaries, it also covers midstream activities such as food processing and logistics, but its core business is retail.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The group’s strategic priorities include strengthening customer-centric management, leveraging scale for procurement and cost efficiency, enhancing store service and product quality, and accelerating digital transformation. Sustainability initiatives focus on carbon neutrality, waste reduction, and community engagement. R&D is not a major focus, but investments are made in IT systems, store automation, and original product development.
categories.revenue_model: USMH generates revenue primarily through direct sales of food and daily necessities at its supermarket stores. Additional income comes from in-house processed foods, private label products, and supporting businesses such as real estate leasing and logistics services. Revenue is recognized at the point of sale to consumers.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: USMH is positioned as the largest supermarket group in the Tokyo metropolitan area, competing with other major Japanese supermarket chains and general merchandise retailers, including Ito-Yokado (Seven & i Holdings), Life Corporation, and regional supermarket operators. The group benefits from its scale, regional dominance, and affiliation with Aeon Group.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending February 2025, consolidated net sales were 793.9 billion yen, with operating profit of 5.98 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 810 million yen. The group operates 660 stores and employs over 9,300 regular employees (plus over 26,000 part-time/temporary staff). Growth in sales was driven by the integration of Inageya, but profitability declined due to rising costs and competitive pressures.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: USMH emphasizes a customer-first philosophy, offering a wide assortment of fresh foods, daily necessities, and original prepared foods tailored to local needs. Its value proposition includes convenience, quality, competitive pricing, and community engagement. The group differentiates itself through scale-driven procurement, in-house food processing, and a strong regional presence in the Tokyo metropolitan area.
